rationale: There are 10 acceptance criteria. The spec adds a new CLI group with five subcommands, a new wire protocol (header and frames) and a persisted worker store. That is one subsystem, so size l rather than xl. The tone is critical because the spec defines a key that equals shell access, a forced-command allowlist and a shared object cache that concurrent jobs write to. A defect in any of these is a security problem or makes gate results wrong.

findings.title: Base branch refs created "in the job tree" are shared by all concurrent jobs
findings.detail: Step 3 says: "In the job tree, create `refs/heads/<name>` at `base.sha`, and also `refs/remotes/origin/<rest>`". The job tree is a `git worktree add` of the shared bare cache `repos/<repo_key>.git`. In git only HEAD, refs/bisect/* and refs/worktree/* are per-worktree. `refs/heads/*` and `refs/remotes/*` live in the common repo. If two jobs for the same repo run at once (the worker has several gate slots, or two coordinators send jobs), both write `refs/heads/main`. If their base shas differ, one job's `git merge-base $NW_BASE HEAD` resolves against the other job's base. That gives wrong affected-test selection or a wrong diff with no error. Step 6 also never deletes these refs, so the next job inherits a stale `main`.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the worktree-per-job checkout with a private repo per job that borrows the cache's objects. Write step 3 as: "`git clone --shared --no-checkout repos/<repo_key>.git <job>/tree` (the objects are read through alternates; refs are private to the job), then `git -C <job>/tree checkout --detach <commit>`, then create `refs/heads/<name>` (and `refs/remotes/origin/<rest>` when `name` is `origin/<rest>`) at `base.sha` inside `<job>/tree`." Change step 6 to "`rm -rf <job>/tree`" in place of `git worktree remove --force`. Add an acceptance criterion: "Two concurrent gate-jobs for the same repo_key with different `base.sha` for the same `base.name` each see their own base in `git rev-parse $NW_BASE`."
findings.acceptance: The Design no longer writes branch refs into the shared cache. An AC and a test case cover two concurrent jobs with different bases.

findings.section: Design › Worker store / gate-job steps / gc
findings.title: Concurrency on the shared cache and have.json is unspecified
findings.detail: Several jobs can run at once on one worker, one per gate slot. Each one `git fetch`es into the same bare repo, sets `refs/nw/have/*` and updates `repos/<repo_key>.have.json`, and step 6 "run[s] `gc`" after every job. The spec has no lock. The read-modify-write of have.json races and can lose last-used times, so `gc` then ages refs out early. A `gc` triggered by job A can delete job B's in-flight `jobs/<job_id>/` (manual `gc --keep-days 0` certainly will) and its refs. Concurrent fetches into one repo can also fail on ref-lock contention.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Design › Worker store: "Each repo cache has a lock file `repos/<repo_key>.lock` (fcntl.flock). The bundle fetch, setting `refs/nw/have/*`, updating `<repo_key>.have.json` (written via temp file and os.replace) and `gc`'s deletions all happen under it. `gc` never deletes a job dir whose `job.lock` is flock-held by a live gate-job; every gate-job holds `jobs/<job_id>/job.lock` from claim until exit." Add a test: `gc --keep-days 0` run while a `sleep` gate job is live leaves that job's dir intact.
findings.acceptance: The spec names the lock and the in-flight-job exemption from gc, and a test covers gc during a live job.

findings.title: gc never prunes objects, so the cache grows without bound
findings.detail: `nw worker gc` "deletes job dirs and `refs/nw/have/*` refs older than N days". Deleting a ref does not free its objects. Nothing runs `git gc --prune` or `git worktree prune` (if worktrees stay). Every bundle's objects accumulate in `repos/<repo_key>.git` forever, yet `info` reports `free_bytes` as if space were managed.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the gc bullet: "... then, under the repo lock, runs `git -C repos/<repo_key>.git gc --prune=now --quiet` for each repo whose refs changed (and `git worktree prune` if worktrees are kept)." Extend the gc acceptance criterion: "after `gc --keep-days 0`, `nw worker have` reports none of the job's shas and `git cat-file -e <commit>` fails in the cache."
findings.acceptance: gc's description includes object pruning, and the AC checks that the objects are gone.

findings.title: Header fields `timeout_s`, `have` and `attempt`, and the 'protocol major' check, have no defined worker behaviour
findings.detail: The header carries `timeout_s`, `have: [...]` and `attempt: 0`, and step 1 validates "protocol major". None of these is defined. It is unclear whether `timeout_s` bounds the whole job, including the slot wait and checkout, or whether only `payload.gate_budget_s` (used as the deadline) applies. The worker's use of `have` and `attempt` is unspecified. The schema string is `nw.job.v1`, and no `protocol` field exists to take a major from. An implementer will guess, and SPEC-0338 will depend on that guess.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a bullet list under the header block: "`timeout_s`: the worker ignores it (it is the coordinator's own wall-clock budget); the gate deadline is `slot hold + payload.gate_budget_s`. `have`: informational, the shas the coordinator assumed present when it cut the bundle; the worker does not read it, and a missing prerequisite surfaces as `error` with `stage: \"checkout\"`. `attempt`: echoed into `job.json` only. Protocol check: `schema` must equal `nw.job.v1`; any other value gives `error` with `stage: \"validate\"`." Alternatively, drop the fields the worker does not need.
findings.acceptance: Every header field has a stated worker behaviour or is removed.

findings.title: The slot_wait test needs a 30 s wait that the subprocess test cannot shorten
findings.detail: `slot_wait` is "emitted once the wait passes 30 s". That is `gate_slots.WAIT_EVENT_S = 30.0`, a module constant (`gate_slots.py:25`). The test runs `nw worker gate-job` as a subprocess, so it cannot monkeypatch the constant. The "held worker slot gives slot_wait/started" case would take at least 30 s per run. The spec also does not say what happens on stdin EOF during the slot wait.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Design step 4: "The 30 s threshold is read from `NW_WORKER_SLOT_WAIT_EVENT_S` (default 30) so tests can lower it. `cancel_event` is passed as `stop=` to `gate_slots.acquire`, so EOF during the wait ends it, and the worker emits `done` with `interrupted: true` and no `started`." In the Test plan, set that variable to 0.5 for the held-slot case and add a case "EOF while waiting for the slot".
findings.acceptance: The held-slot test runs in seconds, and EOF during the slot wait is specified and tested.

findings.title: The forced command's per-subcommand option grammar is not enumerated
findings.detail: "the rest match that subcommand's option grammar" leaves the allowlist to the implementer, and this is the security boundary. The arguments of `have --repo KEY` are not charset-checked either, so `--repo ../../x` could address a path outside `repos/`.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace that phrase with an explicit grammar: "`info` [`--json`]; `have` `--repo` <[A-Za-z0-9._-]+> <[0-9a-f]{40,64}>...; `gate-job` (no arguments); `gc` [`--keep-days` <[0-9]+>]. Any other token is refused." Also state that `have` itself validates `--repo` against the same charset as `repo_key`.
findings.acceptance: ssh-command's accepted argv grammar is listed literally, and the tests cover a `--repo ../x` refusal.

findings.section: Design › gate-job steps (5. Run each gate)
findings.title: Placeholder and environment sources are underspecified
findings.detail: "with placeholders from the worker's tree path" covers only `{worktree}`. `{base}` must be `base.name` (to match `gates.placeholders`), `{spec_id}` and `{campaign}` come from the header, and `NW_BASE` must equal `base.name`, not the sha. The spec also does not say whether gates inherit the worker process's own `os.environ` (PATH, HOME) on top of the allowlist.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the step to: "placeholders `{worktree: <job>/tree, base: base.name, spec_id: header.spec_id, campaign: header.campaign}`; env = the worker process's own environment, plus the allowlisted keys from the header, plus `NW_WORKTREE`, `NW_DATA_DIR`, `NW_CONFIG_DIR` and `tmp_env(<job>/tmp)`. The header's `NW_BASE`, if present, must equal `base.name`, else `error` with `stage: \"validate\"`."
findings.acceptance: Each placeholder and env key has a stated source.

findings.title: Exit codes for normal completion are not stated
findings.detail: Only "exit code 3" for an exception and 2 for ssh-command refusal are given. It is not stated whether gate-job exits 0 after a `done` with `ok: false`, or what it exits on a validate or claim error. The coordinator (SPEC-0338) needs these to tell a transport failure from a gate failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: "gate-job exits 0 after emitting `done` (whatever `ok` is, including `interrupted: true`), 3 after an `error` frame at any stage, and never exits without one of the two frames unless stdout is closed."
findings.acceptance: The exit codes are listed for done, error and interrupted.

findings.title: The docs acceptance criterion has no test plan entry
findings.detail: The AC "`docs/WORKFLOW.md` documents the mandatory dedicated user and the absolute-path key line" is not mentioned in the Test plan.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Test plan: "**Manual:** check that `docs/WORKFLOW.md` has a 'Remote gate worker' section stating the dedicated unprivileged user is mandatory and showing the `command=\"/home/user/.local/bin/nw worker ssh-command\",restrict` key line."
findings.acceptance: Every AC maps to a test plan line.
